title: Bianzhong of Marquis Yi of Zeng
status_note: Excavated in 1978; displayed at the Hubei Provincial Museum.

place.label: Hubei Provincial Museum, Wuhan (excavated at Suizhou)

timeline.event: Burial of Marquis Yi, early Warring States period (UNESCO: about 2,400 years ago, 5th century BCE)

tiers.everyday: These 65 bronze bells from the tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng are about 2,400 years old. Each bell can play two different notes depending on where it is struck.
tiers.student: The Hubei Provincial Museum lists 65 bells (19 niuzhong, 45 yongzhong and one bo bell given by King Hui of Chu) on a 7.48 m rack in three tiers and eight groups, with 3,755 inscribed characters on music theory. Each bell sounds two tones a third apart; the set spans about 5.5 octaves. UNESCO lists it in Memory of the World.

model.label: Chinese zhong are almond-shaped in section; the round profile model would misrepresent them.

unknowns: exact burial year (pinned as approximate 433 BCE from UNESCO's 5th century BCE framing)
